In construction here we use imperial to measure for some reason. I think it's to do with standard heights but fraction are a pain. I don't know what 90 degrees Fahrenheit means however. Good to know both.

It's because in order to change a single thing in construction you have to change the entire system. Drywall is a standard 4x6 sheet (they do have bigger though) It's meant to line up with studs that are set 16inches apart and come to meet in the middle of a 2x4. Light switches are standard 4' off the ground which also falls on the seam between two sheets. The tape that is used to seal drywall is also a set width based on a groove at the top of each board. And that's just for one part of framing. It's one huge interlocking puzzle and you can't just change one piece. Also think about the tools. Every builder / company would have to re purchase anything with a measurement on it. Wrenches, speed squares, screwdrivers, bits, drill bits...
